name: Neal Aronson
current_role: Founder and Managing Partner, Roark Capital Group (Atlanta)
profile: Neal Aronson (b. 1965) founded Atlanta private-equity firm Roark Capital in 2001 and remains its majority owner. Roark specialises in franchised brands and owns Subway, Arby's, Jimmy John's, Sonic, Dunkin' and Baskin-Robbins (via Inspire Brands), having done many of the restaurant industry's biggest deals of the past decade.
interesting_fact: Roark Capital is named after Howard Roark, the uncompromising architect-hero of Ayn Rand's The Fountainhead.
deep_cut_fact: Before Roark, he co-founded U.S. Franchise Systems in 1995 with his uncle Mike Leven (ex-Holiday Inn president), growing a 27-hotel regional chain (Microtel) into the 10th-largest US hotel franchisor with 1,100+ properties before selling to Hyatt's Pritzkers in 2000. He began his career in Drexel Burnham Lambert's corporate finance department.
notes: Low public profile; best route is Roark's media contact at Joele Frank. Franchise focus (restaurants, services) — not energy, but large real-asset/consumer deal-maker.

name: Martua Sitorus
current_role: Co-founder, KPN Corp (formerly Gama Corp), Indonesia; co-founder of Wilmar International (left board 2018)
profile: Born in Pematangsiantar, North Sumatra, Martua Sitorus co-founded Wilmar International with Kuok Khoon Hong in 1991, growing it into one of the world's largest palm oil traders. He left Wilmar's board in 2018 and now runs KPN Corp with his brother Ganda, spanning palm plantations, property (Gama Land), cement (Cemindo Gemilang) and hospitals (Murni Sadar).
interesting_fact: A former economics student, he traded shrimp as a teenager before switching to palm oil; the name 'Gama' comes from the founders' first names, Ganda and Martua.
deep_cut_fact: His Medan hospital, Murni Teguh Memorial Hospital, is named after his mother, Murni Teguh, and was launched on the date 12/12/2012. His Gama group also built Jakarta's 64-storey Gama Tower, described as Indonesia's tallest building.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contact found (kpncorp.com is a parked domain). Possible routes: listed affiliates Cemindo Gemilang or Murni Sadar investor relations via IDX filings. Energy angle: palm oil/biodiesel, cement.

name: Gerry Harvey
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, Harvey Norman Holdings (Australia)
profile: Gerry Harvey (b. 1939) co-founded Harvey Norman with Ian Norman in 1982 after their first chain, Norman Ross, was sold; it now sells furniture, electricals and bedding across Australia and 100+ overseas stores (NZ, Singapore, Malaysia, Slovenia, Ireland, UK). His wife Katie Page runs the business as CEO, while he remains executive chairman, a vocal media commentator and a major thoroughbred breeder.
interesting_fact: He owns Baramul Stud, has one of the world's largest thoroughbred portfolios (600+ horses) and co-owns the Magic Millions bloodstock auction.
deep_cut_fact: He started out selling vacuum cleaners and fridges door-to-door for Goodwins of Newtown, where he met Ian Norman; the pair opened their first Sydney store in 1961. He dropped out of university and has said: 'I always wanted to be a farmer.'
notes: Very media-accessible; frequently gives interviews to Australian business press and radio. No published press email found; company contact page or ASX company secretary are the routes.
